title: China Targets AI-Linked Jobs With New Employment Initiative
source_used: Global Times (same State Council press conference); Bloomberg page blocked, headline only
key_facts: Li Zhong, vice minister of Human Resources and Social Security, spoke at a State Council Information Office press conference on Saturday 10 Oct 2026.
He said the ministry will launch initiatives to promote employment amid the development of artificial intelligence.
China created 10.52 million new urban jobs in the first nine months of 2026, 87.7 percent of the annual target.
The average surveyed urban unemployment rate was 5.2 percent in the first eight months of the year.
The ministry also plans skills training under the 'Skills Brighten the Future' campaign and support for youth, graduate and migrant-worker employment.
Bloomberg's headline describes the plan as a new employment initiative targeting AI-linked jobs; its text was not readable.
quote_evidence: The ministry will also launch initiatives to promote employment amid the development of artificial intelligence, provide skills training under the "Skills Brighten the Future" campaign, support migrant workers' employment, improve the provision of high-quality public employment services, and promote the integrated development of human resources services with other sectors.

China created a total of 10.52 million new urban jobs in the first nine months of 2026, fulfilling 87.7 percent of its annual target, Li Zhong, vice minister of Human Resources and Social Security, said at a press conference held by the State Council Information Office on Saturday.
why_it_matters_hint: China's government says it will act on AI's effect on work, but gives no detail on what the measures are.
notes: Bloomberg (403, robot check) was not readable; details come from Global Times, a state-run outlet, which reports the ministry's own statement. No specifics of the AI employment initiative were found in either outlet.
